Santosh vs State Of U.P. on 17 July, 2023
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
?Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc:141804
Court No. - 70
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 30888 of 2023

Applicant :- Santosh
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.

Counsel for Applicant :- Vijay Singh Sengar
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.
Supplementary affidavit filed today on behalf of the applicant, is taken on record.

2. Heard Sri Vijay Singh Sengar, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Imran Khan, learned AGA for the State-respondent.
3. The instant application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No.
407 of 2022, under Sections 498A, 304B IPC and 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station Kotwali Orai, District Jalaun, during pendency of the trial in the court below.

4. FIR of the present case was lodged against the applicant and his brother & mother and according to the FIR, marriage of the applicant was performed with the deceased on 13.2.2018 but after marriage, applicant and his family members tortured the deceased for want of a motorcycle and Rs.
50,000/- and on 9.8.2022, informant received an information that his sister i.e. deceased has been murdered by the applicant and his family members.

Santosh vs State Of U.P. on 17 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133373512/
1 5.

Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that although initially there was allegation of demand of dowry and harassment against the applicant in the FIR and in the statement of the prosecution witnesses recorded during investigation but when informant and his witnesses appeared before the trial court then they did not support the version of the FIR and they have declared hostile.

6. He further submitted that there is no evidence on record at present against the applicant that applicant ever demanded dowry or harassed the deceased, therefore, applicant who is in jail in the present matter since 28.8.2022, may be released on bail.
7. He further submitted that post mortem report of the deceased shows that she committed suicide.

He next argued, deceased always insisted to live with the applicant in Delhi and when applicant could not accept her proposal then she committed suicide.
8.
Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail but could not dispute the fact that all the prosecution witnesses of fact including informant have declared hostile during trial.
9. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

10. Although, applicant is husband of the deceased but during trial, witnesses of fact including informant have declared hostile and they categorically stated before the trial court that there was no demand of dowry.
Applicant is in jail in the present matter since 28.8.2022 i.e. for last almost a year, therefore, in my view, applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
11. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

12. Let the applicant-Santosh be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.
(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
13.
In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.

Santosh vs State Of U.P. on 17 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133373512/
2 14.

It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.

Order Date :- 17.7.2023/Ankita  Santosh vs State Of U.P. on 17 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133373512/
